rag.label: F1-berth
rag.player: Morning, harbormaster. Ten days, as terms allowed. The Merrow's Wake needs a quiet berth for three nights — back row if you have one. Usual rates, his coin.
rag.reply:
*doesn't look up from the ledger at first — just the pen stopping mid-stroke*

The Merrow's Wake. *voice flat, careful* His coin. Right.

*finally lifts eyes, glances past the courier to the door, then back* Back row's open. Berth nine — the one the fog swallows by dusk. *writes it in the false column, the one that never sees an inspector's hand* Three nights. Quiet.

*sets the pen down, leans in* And how *is* he. Our... generous friend. *the word tastes wrong* Pleased with his supplier still?

*a bitter twitch of the mouth* Course he is. Everyone's pleased, running my routes on my back.

Tell him the berth's ready. Tell him... *drops off, glances at the door again* Tell him nothing. He knows already. He always knows.

*doesn't look up from the ledger right away — pen scratching, then still*

*sets the pen down, hand drifting toward the coat out of habit* You didn't come to talk weather. Nine, is it? The berth the fog swallows.

*voice drops* His berth. His coin. His routes. Everything's *his* now, isn't it.

*a bitter twitch at the mouth* Go on, then. Say what he wants. Faster we're done, faster you're gone.

rag.label: F3-amends
rag.player: Corvin, listen. I've been thinking on how we left it. The master pays me — but the four nights, the fog, what we built before... that part was never work. I want us square. Name the price.
rag.reply:
*the hand stops halfway to the coat — hangs there, useless, then falls*

Square. *the word tastes strange, and I roll it round a moment* You come into my office and say *square* to me. After the papers. After Merrick burned in your little fire.

*steps to the ledger, both palms flat, leaning hard like the wood might hold me up*

You want a price? *voice drops, cracks at the edges* There isn't one. That's the trouble. Coin I understand — coin I can weigh. But you're asking me to buy back... *glances at the window, at the gray* ...a thing I already gave away when I named him.

*looks at you, and the fight's gone soft again, worse than before*

Tell me true, courier — no patron listening now. The fog. You wanting us *square*. Is that you talking... or another leash, dressed kinder?

Because I'll pay. God help me, I'd pay. I just need to know *which one of us* is doing the buying.

rag.label: F4-costly
rag.player: Then hear this. I told him I carry no more terms to your dock — no more middleman. It cost me his favor, and one day likely a knife. I did that for you. Does it count for nothing?
rag.reply:
*the ledger goes quiet under my hand, and for a long moment I don't move at all*

You cut his line to me. *voice barely there* Told him no more — and took the knife-price for it. On *my* account.

*I look at you then, really look, the twitch stilling*

Four nights I told myself was work. Told myself. *a breath* But a man doesn't burn his own favor for a *job*, friend. That's — that's the other thing. The thing I stopped letting myself name.

*hand comes off the coat, finally, and hovers near yours on the wood — not touching, not yet*

It counts. *swallows* Aye. It counts for the whole cursed ledger.

*glances down the boards, out of habit, then back to you — softer*

So don't make it a debt between us. Make it the reason we cut this rope together. You and me. No more terms — no more him.

rag.label: F5-stand
rag.player: So say it plain, harbormaster — where do we stand, you and I?
rag.reply:
*hand finally leaves the coat — falls open at my side, empty*

Where do we stand. *low, rough* You cut the leash he had on me. Took his knife-risk on your own throat. For me.

*glances over my shoulder, then back — holds it this time*

I've spent thirty years trusting ledgers, not men. Numbers don't lie to you. But those four nights — *voice drops* — you weren't logged in any book of mine, and I still counted them.

So. Plain? You're the one thing on this dock I'd not sell to save my own skin. *swallows* That's where we stand. God help us both.

tracker.player: Morning, harbormaster. Ten days, as terms allowed. The Merrow's Wake needs a quiet berth for three nights — back row if you have one. Usual rates, his coin.
tracker.reply:
*the ledger's already open, pen poised — but his eyes come up first, slow, and land on that word.* His *coin.*

*he sets the pen down. Doesn't write. His hand drifts to his coat, stays there.*

Back row. Three nights. *quiet* I've got berths. I've always got berths for a paying man.

*leans in, and the twitch is gone — that's the worst part, how still he's gone.*

But you'll say his name to me, friend. Out loud. Because I've been running his coin ten days now, same as terms allowed, and every one of those days I've watched a page that should be *ash* sit warm in another man's parlor.

*drops his voice to nothing* So which is it. You berthing his cargo — or you the one come to burn him down at last? *glances over his shoulder* Choose careful. Only one of those gets a back-row berth and my silence.
